page: Amazon Web Services r6in.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processor running at 3.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, providing 4 vCPUs derived from 2 dedicated physical cores via hyperthreading. Memory is configured at 32.0 GB of DDR4 running at 3 GHz, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio. The processor includes hardware acceleration flags such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The instance does not include integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes, nor does it contain any GPUs.

Benchmark testing demonstrates average single-threaded efficiency paired with lower multi-threaded throughput, constrained by the 4 vCPU topology. Single-core evaluations, including Geekbench single-core (1605.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (28.03 GB/sec), place within average ranges, as do PassMark memory (2073.98) and PassMark encryption (3606.04). In contrast, multi-threaded results such as the stress-ng multi-core score (3860.76), Geekbench multi-core score (3420.0), and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (19.45 GB/sec) score in the lower percentiles across evaluated cloud tiers.

In operational testing, the instance achieved a static web serving throughput of 6.36 GB/sec backed by a baseline network bandwidth of 6 Gbps. Key-value operations showed Redis SET performance reaching 4.02 million operations per second, while small-model LLM inference generated 96.82 tokens per second. Given its memory-to-vCPU allocation, the instance suits memory-resident workloads such as medium-sized caching layers, in-memory databases, and data processing services that demand dedicated memory capacity without heavy parallel compute requirements.
description: Amazon Web Services r6in.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro System. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8375C processor with x86_64 architecture running at 3.5 GHz, it supplies 4 vCPUs across 2 dedicated physical cores and 32.0 GB of DDR4 system memory. There is no bundled local storage or GPU hardware. The networking layer provides a baseline bandwidth of 6 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations reflect solid single-threaded metrics, including an average Geekbench single-core score of 1605.0 and PassMark memory score of 2073.98, while multi-threaded capacity remains constrained by the limited core count. Serving up to 4.02 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.36 GB/sec of static web throughput, the r6in.xlarge fits memory-heavy applications, distributed caching layers, and in-memory datastores that do not depend on broad multi-threaded compute.
